source.edition: Sinho Chewi, Lectures on Optimization, arXiv:2605.07006v1
source.summary: Section 3 assumes twice continuously differentiable objectives and actual gradient updates. Exercise 3.2 asks for the endpoint spectral bound, optimal constant step 2/(alpha+beta), and contraction factor (kappa-1)/(kappa+1). Exercise 3.3 asks for explicit iterates of a positive-definite quadratic and assessment of Section 3 sharpness. Definition 3.2 relates quadratic moduli to extremal eigenvalues.

proposed_statement.parameters: real 0 < alpha <= beta; arbitrary real constant step h; natural N
proposed_statement.witness: Choose mu=alpha if |1-h*beta|<=|1-h*alpha|, otherwise mu=beta; f_mu(x)=mu*x^2/2 on R; x0=1 and xstar=0.
required_certificates: actual beta-smooth upper model with gradient f_mu, or actual Lipschitz gradient plus compiled model adapter
0 is a global minimizer and x0 has norm one (hence is nonzero)
proposed_statement.preferred_quantifier_order: forall alpha beta, 0<alpha -> alpha<=beta -> forall h, exists mu in {alpha,beta}, all objective certificates and forall N, exact equality and lower bound
proposed_statement.minimal_quantifier_order: forall alpha beta h N, admissible parameters -> exists mu with objective certificates and the N-step equality/lower bound
proposed_statement.optimal_step: At h=2/(alpha+beta), either endpoint gives norm(T_h^[N](1))=q^N. Existing general endpoint upper bound plus iteration establishes uniform optimality for nonnegative fixed steps.

scalar_vs_fixed_matrix.scalar_suffices: Yes, for class-level worst-case constant-step distance sharpness. The adversarial objective may depend on h; its selection need not depend on N. alpha and beta are valid lower/upper curvature bounds, not necessarily both tight.
scalar_vs_fixed_matrix.not_supported: When alpha<beta, a one-dimensional scalar quadratic has intrinsic tight condition number 1. Do not identify beta/alpha as the intrinsic condition number of this witness or claim its Hessian has both endpoints.
scalar_vs_fixed_matrix.fixed_2d_option: For the stronger quantifier exists f forall h exists unit x0 forall N, use the single objective (alpha*x1^2+beta*x2^2)/2 with diag(alpha,beta), and select an endpoint basis vector according to h. This objective has exact extremal curvatures alpha,beta. It is optional for the bounded class-level theorem.

route: Construct the scalar quadratic with mu>0 and actual differentiability.
Prove exact mu curvature/smoothness then weaken constants using alpha<=mu<=beta, or use direct exact quadratic remainder for both bounds.
Certify zero as global minimizer and one as unit start.
Instantiate existing quadratic_eigenmode at H=mu times identity and x=1; do not reprove iteration or eigenvector powers.
Select the endpoint attaining the maximum by total order.
Reuse optimal_gradient_step second conjunct for q<=M (or extract a standalone scalar envelope lemma if that reduces artificial objective coupling). Raise nonnegative quantities to N.
At balanced step simplify both endpoint absolute values to q; keep full-section and oracle claims open.

truth_boundary: An attained lower bound against any one fixed scalar step does not lower-bound arbitrary first-order algorithms, adaptive or varying step sequences, or accelerated methods.
The source Exercise 3.3 asks about all section results; this target resolves only the distance endpoint bound/optimal fixed-step comparison, not function-value or stationarity sharpness.
Arbitrary h is permitted for exact evolution and lower bounds, including h<0 and unstable h. This is not an arbitrary-step convergence statement.
N=0 uses the conventional zeroth power 1, including q=0; alpha=beta gives q=0 and one-step exact optimization at h=1/alpha.
alpha=0 is deliberately excluded to retain positive-definite source witnesses and source condition-number interpretation.
No compact spectral endpoint existence theorem in general Hilbert spaces is needed or asserted.
